C0.quote: individual agents report their preferences into a collective decision
C0.note: Proposes a procedure (voting by axioms) for aggregating reported preference profiles into collective outcomes.

C1.quote: Section 4 is devoted to algorithmic and Section 5 to axiomatic results
C1.note: Section 3 structural properties and Section 5 axiomatic results outnumber the complexity/SAT results of Section 4.

C2.1.quote: assigns to each agent i ∈ N a (reported) preference

C2.2.note: L(X) is the set of strict linear orders.

C2.3.note: Preferences are referred to as something agents have and report, though not given separate notation.

C2.4.note: IDS and IDU fit about equally: the text implies agents report their own preferences, without a reason or separate notation; the first-listed code was chosen.

C3.2.note: Weak statement, consistent with the C2.4 code.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost, distortion or intensity notions are used for voters.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: Pareto: If profile R is such that all agents prefer
C5.1.note: The Pareto axiom is defined and used only in illustrative examples; no formal result evaluates rules or outcomes by efficiency or welfare.

VOT.quote_behav: agents expressing a preference in a given situation
VOT.note: Voters only supply a fixed profile.

DES.note: Choice of the axiom corpus is discussed informally but no designer objective is modelled.

claims.quote: it is most suited to high-stakes situations
we require any decision taken to stand on sound normative grounds
The decisions taken will be appropriate only if the axioms are.

C9.1.note: Claims concern the suitability of the approach for real decisions.

C9.2.note: The claims are about the procedure's normative grounding; it is unclear whether they require assumptions relating reported profiles to held preferences.
